## Answer
The late-delivery rate increased from 4.5% to 6.56%, which is a significant rise. This could be due to a combination of factors, including changes in delivery performance across specific sellers, regions, or product categories.

## Findings
- Late-delivery rate increased by 2.06 percentage points (from 4.5% to 6.56%).
- Overdue undelivered orders decreased from 121 to 84.
- Cancellation rate increased by 0.29 percentage points (from 0.29% to 0.58%).
- Average delivery time slightly decreased from 11.4 to 11.3 days.
- Average promised delivery window decreased by 0.8 days (from 24.3 to 23.5 days).
- Average order value increased slightly from R$167.25 to R$167.78.
- Low-review rate decreased from 12.99% to 11.9%.

## Investigate first
- Check the performance of sellers with the highest late-delivery rates in May 2018.
- Analyze delivery performance by region to identify any geographic trends.
- Review the product categories with the highest late-delivery rates to determine if specific items are more prone to delays.

## Limitations
- The data does not provide granular details on specific sellers, regions, or product categories.
- There is no information on the reasons for late deliveries or cancellations.
- The data is limited to aggregated metrics and does not include customer feedback or order-specific details.
